output.title: The quiet cost of model deprecation
output.body:
If you are weighing automation against another hire, don’t just ask what it costs to build. Ask what it costs to keep working when the model underneath it changes, gets retired, or becomes awkward to use.

That shows up in ordinary workflows: customer-inquiry triage, lead qualification, invoice handling, or document sorting. On day one, the workflow can look fine. Later, a model change or pricing change may mean you need to adjust prompts, retest the flow, or fall back to manual work. That is not a catastrophe. It is a maintenance decision, and it belongs in the business case.

The practical next step is simple: before you approve a pilot, ask one blunt question. If the underlying model is upgraded, retired, or repriced, does this workflow keep running as designed, or do we need to rebuild parts of it and approve that spend again? If the answer is unclear, you do not have a complete plan yet.

Automation is easiest to justify when the workflow is stable and the owner understands the upkeep. Otherwise, the cheapest entry price can hide the harder part.
